pr_title: Mqtt fan feature for resetting current speed `percentage` or `preset_mode`
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Implement a feature to allow resetting `preset_mode` or `percentage` to `None` by using a specially defined payload.
Two new attributes are introduced that allow to customize this special reset payload.

- `payload_reset_percentage` (abbreviation `pl_rst_pct`). Defaults to `None`. When this payload is received on the `percentage_state_topic`, the current state or attribute `percentage` (and legacy attribute `speed`, if configured) will be reset to `None`.
- `payload_reset_preset_mode` (abbreviation `pl_rst_pr_mode`). Defaults to `None`. When this special payload is received on `preset_mode_state_topic`, the current state or attribute `preset_mode` will be reset no `None`.

This PR also fixes a new bug found where self.async_write_ha_state() was at async_set_speed() or async_set_preset_mode() called without optimistic mode being enabled.

Hey there @emontnemery, mind taking a look at this pull request as its been labeled with an integration (`mqtt`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L303) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Hi,
Can you explain what the use case of resetting internal components states to `None`?
The `self._preset_mode`, `self._percentage` and `self._speed` stores internal states of the entity.

> 
> 
> Hi,
> Can you explain what the use case of resetting internal components states to `None`?
> The `self._preset_mode`, `self._percentage` and `self._speed` stores internal states of the entity.

The (https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/fan/)[documentation] says that

> Manually setting a speed must disable a preset mode. If it is possible to set a percentage speed manually without disabling the preset mode, create a switch or service to represent the mode.

So the device it self must be able to reset a `preset_mode` if it became invalid due to setting a speed.
When setting a preset like `auto` is selected the last speed set could become invalid and should be able to reset (see also linked issue https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/50435).
Discussed this with @emontnemery.
@bdraco can you help confirm it makes sense from a base entity point of view to allow resetting `preset_mode` or `percentage` to `None`?

> 
> The ([https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/fan/)[documentation]](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/fan/)%5Bdocumentation%5D) says that
> 
> > Manually setting a speed must disable a preset mode. If it is possible to set a percentage speed manually without disabling the preset mode, create a switch or service to represent the mode.
> 
> So the device it self must be able to reset a `preset_mode` if it became invalid due to setting a speed.
> When setting a preset like `auto` is selected the last speed set could become invalid and should be able to reset (see also linked issue #50435).
> Discussed this with @emontnemery.

I understand the functionality requirement, however I think that it should be looked from a user perspective, a user does not know the internal implementation or that there is a variable that stores states and `None` is an invalid state. If manually setting a speed must disable preset mode than we have to implement this functionality inside the component, without the user needs to call something to reset it.
Anyhow would be good to edit the PR description to explain what you wrote in the comment, when reading the description there it explains what is implemented but not the use case for it, I think a `yaml` example of such configuration will also help.

> If manually setting a speed must disable preset mode than we have to implement this functionality inside the component, without the user needs to call something to reset it.

Any such logic should only be there when the MQTT fan is in optimistic mode though, otherwise it must be the remote device (not the user) which is responsible for updating the entity's state.

The goal of the requirement is to avoid a case like the following:

- fan is in auto preset mode 
- user manually sets the speed to 50%
- auto preset mode remains in effect and it shortly changes the speed to 75%
- user wonders why their change didn't take effect
- user sets speed to 50%
- auto preset mode changes speed back to 75%

...


If that can't happen with MQTT there isn't a need to set anything to None

@bdraco Home Assisstant's MQTT integration defines a protocol where service calls are translated to MQTT messages and received MQTT messages are translated to state changes. I don't think the MQTT integration should make assumptions about how the MQTT integration acts on received messages, but it should make it possible to update the state as intended by the base component.

> @bdraco Home Assisstant's MQTT integration defines a protocol where service calls are translated to MQTT messages and received MQTT messages are translated to state changes. I don't think the MQTT integration should make assumptions about how the MQTT integration acts on received messages, but it should make it possible to update the state as intended by the base component.

That makes sense to me.  MQTT is a bit of a special case since it doesn't know about the underlying fan implementation

> MQTT is a bit of a special case since it doesn't know about the underlying fan implementation

Yes, that's a better way to put it!

With that in mind, do you think this PR has the right approach?

issue_context.title: MQTT Fan does not clear preset mode when setting speed percentage
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Hi @jbouwh - one more MQTT Fan bug to report. Identified by @mwav3 in relation to that same zigbee fan I was looking at last week: https://github.com/Koenkk/zigbee2mqtt/issues/7318#issuecomment-837302736

The bug is that setting a percentage does not clear the current preset_mode (and possibly vice versa?).

Since the 99432 fan that we've been working with only _has_ one preset (and 4 speeds): once we have set the `smart` preset once, there's currently no way to clear it, nor to set it again and get another MQTT message to fire, e.g. by going to a speed and back to a preset. I believe this is due to the preset still being applied throughout.

I _think_ this is a bug in the MQTT fan entity, since the general HA [fan entity](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/fan/#preset-modes) says:
> Manually setting a speed must disable a preset mode. If it is possible to set a percentage speed manually without disabling the preset mode, create a switch or service to represent the mode.

I tried to put together a patch locally, but wasn't sure whether how this should impact optimistic mode or the legacy speeds support.

Could you take a look? 

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2021.5.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

MQTT fan

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/fan.mqtt/

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_
comments:
Hey there @emontnemery, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`mqtt`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L303) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

A `preset_mode` is not a speed. I cannot see why a `preset_mode` should be disabled when speed changes.
If you have only one preset, I would recommend using a switch tuning it on and off, or add and an extra preset_modes to be able to change between the default and availailable preset mode.
@bdraco what is your opinion concerning this issue? Should i implement `preset_mode` = None after a `percentage` change. To my opinion the fans speed could change automatically and report back the actual speed where a preset `auto` was set.
Normally the mqtt device should take care of reporting back the actual state / preset_mode. The last value received is the actual mode. Since a preset_mode is not a speed it shoud not be effected by speed changes.
The docs are a bit unclear on this. It probably should say `Manually setting a speed must disable a preset mode if the preset mode automatically controls the fan speed.`

> 
> 
> The docs are a bit unclear on this. It probably should say `Manually setting a speed must disable a preset mode if the preset mode automatically controls the fan speed.`

@bdraco What do you mean with 'disable'. Receiving None over a mqtt is not supported, since value templates with rendering a value from json will result in an empty response that is to be ignored.

Yep, I definitely agree that the difference between speeds and modes is tricky... it's a big challenge trying to define an architecture model for all of Home Assistant that is generic enough to encompass all physical fans out there in the world :) 

Here's a table I put together to summarize what can be expressed in the Zigbee protocol, how that might look for a generic Zigbee fan represented in Home Assistant "speeds + presets" model, and then finally what the Zigbee values mean **specifically** to this 99432 fan, and how _those_ values might be mapped to Home Assistant:

|Zigbee HVAC FanMode Attribute|Zigbee Description|Generic Fan HA Discovery|99432 Meaning|99432 HA Discovery|
|-|-|-|-|-|
|0x00|Off|State: Off|Off|State: Off|
|0x01|Low|Speed: 1|Low|Speed: 1|
|0x02|Medium|Speed: 2|Medium|Speed: 2|
|0x03|High|Speed: 3|High|Speed: 3|
|0x04|On|State: On|Very High|Speed: 4|
|0x05|Auto (the fan speed is self-regulated)|Preset: auto|(unused)|--|
|0x06|Smart (when the heated/cooled space is occupied, the fan is always on)|Preset: smart|"Comfort Breeze"|Preset: Smart|

The fan has only this single control and single state variable - a value 0 through 6, mapped to a single MQTT topic - and although the "smart" mode of this fan (called "Comfort Breeze" in their marketing) will internally be changing the fan speed up and down... it does not report that state externally. It only reports that it is in `smart`.

So my real question underlying all of this is... How to model this fan?

Here, I was trying to achieve "4 speeds plus 1 (mutually exclusive) preset"... but perhaps that is not the right way to think of this fan since all of those are one single setting.

Maybe it should remain as "5 mutually exclusive presets" and skip the percentage slider?

A light clears an effect when changing a color, so the effect can then be selected again - Per the code here - https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/004fa63dbeaf3a2ce285e917c0986ec7174e8b19/homeassistant/components/hyperion/light.py

```
# As we want to preserve brightness control for effects (e.g. to reduce the
# brightness for V4L), we need to persist the effect that is in flight, so
# subsequent calls to turn_on will know the keep the effect enabled.
# Unfortunately the Home Assistant UI does not easily expose a way to remove a
# selected effect (there is no 'No Effect' option by default). Instead, we
# create a new fake effect ("Solid") that is always selected by default for
# showing a solid color. This is the same method used by WLED.
```

Can a similar approach somehow work here?

We should not have any logic in the MQTT fan component which writes the states unless it's in optimistic mode which I assume it isn't when used by zigbee2mqtt? It's up to zigbee2mqtt to send correct state updates.

I chatted a little bit with @jbouwh by email (Thank you!), and I think an idea that he and @mwav3 have raised will make the most sense:

**Problem:** There is no path through `preset_mode_received` that will result in setting `self._preset_mode = None`. So: For this fan with only one preset mode... Once the preset mode has been activated, it cannot be deactivated. Nor can it be activated _again_ since Home Assistant believes it is still set to the same value.

**Workaround:** We will create a fake "`normal`" preset mode that exists only in the MQTT fan template definitions.
This is NOT a real state that the device can be placed in or is aware of... but since there is no mechanism in the MQTT fan to go back to `None`, we will instead use the `preset_mode_value_template` to interpret all non-`smart` values (for example, "`medium`") as this imaginary `normal` preset instead. We will use a `preset_mode_command_template` to avoid actually exposing that `normal` value to zigbee2mqtt.

It would behave like this:
|Zigbee state|Zigbee and MQTT value|99432 state|`state_value_template`|`percentage_value_template`|`preset_mode_value_template`|
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
|0|`off`|Off|OFF|0|`normal`|
|1|`low`|Low|ON|1|`normal`|
|2|`medium`|Medium|ON|2|`normal`|
|3|`high`|High|ON|3|`normal`|
|4|`on`|Very High|ON|4|`normal`|
|6|`smart`|Comfort Breeze|ON|4|`smart`|

@emontnemery Hopefully that helps to answer your question - I do agree with you, MQTT fan entity should **not** be making its own state changes except in optimistic mode. Here, the problem is that the real state change (on the fan and in the Zigbee protocol) is from `self._preset_mode = "smart"` to `self._preset_mode = None`, and there is no MQTT message that can make this happen.

I think the workaround above is very reasonable compromise for this fan, however, and results in a good Home Assistant UI experience (note the `fan_mode` attribute reflecting the one true state of the zigbee fan at any point in time):
![fan_modes](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1765921/118077017-e850f800-b378-11eb-833d-273971bcb4d8.gif)
(If this sounds agreeable, by the way @jbouwh / @emontnemery , then I will propose that we close this bug with no code change, and I can add the `normal` workaround on the zigbee2mqtt side)

For reference, the YAML to accomplish the workaround looks like this:
```yaml
fan:
  - platform: mqtt
    name: "Test Fan"
    command_topic: "zigbee2mqtt/living_room_fan/set/fan_state"
    availability:
      - topic: "zigbee2mqtt/bridge/state"
    json_attributes_topic: "zigbee2mqtt/living_room_fan"
    state_topic: "zigbee2mqtt/living_room_fan"
    state_value_template: "{{ value_json.fan_state }}"
    unique_id: "0x0022a30000423fc6_fan_test"
    speed_range_min: 1
    speed_range_max: 4
    percentage_state_topic: "zigbee2mqtt/living_room_fan"
    percentage_value_template: "{{ {'off': 0, 'low': 1, 'medium': 2, 'high': 3, 'on': 4, 'smart': 2}[value_json.fan_mode] | default('') }}"
    percentage_command_topic: "zigbee2mqtt/living_room_fan/set/fan_mode"
    percentage_command_template: "{{ {0: 'off', 1: 'low', 2: 'medium', 3: 'high', 4: 'on'}[value] | default('')}}"
    preset_mode_state_topic: "zigbee2mqtt/living_room_fan"
    preset_mode_value_template: "{{ 'smart' if value_json.fan_mode == 'smart' else 'normal' }}"
    preset_mode_command_template: "{{ value if value == 'smart' else 'medium' }}"
    preset_mode_command_topic: "zigbee2mqtt/living_room_fan/set/fan_mode"
    preset_modes:
      - "normal"
      - "smart"
  ```

I have been discussing with @emontnemery as well, about an alternative in resetting the preset modes. My idea was to introduce a preset_mode_reset_payload. Received after rendering if this payload is seen it will reset the current preset. In fact we need to decide if this would be the less disruptive solution without breaking value templates functionality. @emontnemery What will have your preference?

The output of templates is actually evaluated. If the template returns the string "None", that will be evaluated to None.
So I think something like this may work:
```py
            preset_mode = self._value_templates[ATTR_PRESET_MODE](msg.payload)
            if preset_mode == "":
                _LOGGER.debug("Ignoring empty preset_mode from '%s'", msg.topic)
                return
            if preset_mode is not None and preset_mode not in self.preset_modes:
                _LOGGER.warning(
                    "'%s' received on topic %s. '%s' is not a valid preset mode",
                    msg.payload,
                    msg.topic,
                    preset_mode,
                )
                return
```

Edit: `async_render_with_possible_json_value` doesn't evaluate the template output, so this doesn't work
The linked PR implements a special payload (default is 'None') to enable resetting `preset_mode` or `percentage` (and speed) over the state topics.
Thanks @jbouwh , @emontnemery for all the ideas & discussion here! I will take up this capability on the zigbee2mqtt side to model the zigbee fan 😄
